subject: MAP: Data-handling checkpoint — retention, logs & PHI scope
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline@bluehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Data-handling checkpoint — retention, logs & PHI scope

Caroline — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) items focused on data handling so we can unstick procurement and security review: 

Key ask (from BlueHealth): confirm how Redwood will store, log, and retain data associated with inference requests that contain PHI/PII.

Proposed MAP milestone (draft):
- Milestone: "Data Classification & Retention Requirements"
  - Owner (BlueHealth): provide definitive list of data classes considered PHI/PII and the retention policy by class (e.g., 90 days session data / 13 months audit logs).
  - Owner (Redwood): provide audit-log sample, retention options & configurable policy, and certs/evidence (SOC2 report extract).
  - Dependencies: vendor Qs answered, procurement terms (retention SLA), and network diagram for private deployment if chosen.
  - Target date: 2027-05-15 (aligns with procurement timeline)

- Milestone: "Audit trail & Access Evidence"
  - Owner (Redwood - Monica): sample audit log, schema, TTL/archival options, redaction controls for PII, and evidence of log integrity (hashing/immutable storage pattern).
  - Owner (BlueHealth): confirm required retention window and list of roles that require access to logs.
  - Dependencies: confirmation of where logs land (customer-managed S3 vs Redwood-managed), any regulatory hold requirements.

- Milestone: "PHI scoping for endpoints"
  - Owner (BlueHealth): identify which API endpoints will carry PHI and which will be tokenized/hashed client-side.
  - Owner (Redwood - Security): provide recommended architecture for PHI minimization and encryption keyflow.

Immediate asks from us:
1) Can you send the spreadsheet with the data elements you consider PHI/PII (a quick CSV is perfect).
2) Confirm whether state retention law (California/other) requires >12 months for any class — if so flag it.
3) Is BlueHealth okay with Redwood sending a redacted audit-log sample or do you need a synthetic version?

I attached the MAP draft we referenced on the call (redwood_map_draft_v2.pdf) and will attach an audit log sample after Monica curates it. If the targets/dates above look off, let me know and we’ll align.

Next step: I’ll follow up with the updated MAP (table view) tomorrow; Monica will attach the sample logs and Neha will chime on security controls.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
---
[Attachment: redwood_map_draft_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 428 KB)]

From: Caroline Hayes <caroline@bluehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueHealth Procurement <procurement@bluehealth.com>, Daniel Ortiz <dan.ortiz@bluehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Data-handling checkpoint — retention, logs & PHI scope

Thanks Markus — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Attached is the CSV with our current data-class list and which items we treat as PHI (columns: field_name, is_phi, example). See bluehealth_data_classes.csv. We flagged MRN, patient_name, insurance_number, device_serial as PHI; hashed tokens and telemetry are non-PHI.
2) Retention: per our legal team, audit logs related to PHI access must be kept for 13 months. Session-level telemetry (non-PHI) can be 90 days.
3) About logs: we prefer a redacted sample first; we can share a small redacted extract to validate schema. Full raw logs will require an MSA/S3 bucket arrangement.

Also looping procurement — they asked for the expected evidence list for the security review: SOC2 Type II, data flow diagram, and the sample audit log schema. Can Redwood confirm which of these you can provide immediately?

We are comfortable with the target date 2027-05-15 as long as procurement has the evidence before 2027-04-20.

Quick note: for PHI endpoints, our initial plan is to route through a private VPC (if possible) to keep network egress inside our account. Please indicate if Redwood supports customer-managed log buckets for audit retention.

Thanks —
Caroline Hayes
Head of Engineering, BlueHealth
---
[Attachment: bluehealth_data_classes.csv (text/csv, 3 KB)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline@bluehealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Data-handling checkpoint — retention, logs & PHI scope

Caroline — great, received the CSV (thank you). I attached a redacted sample audit log (audit-log-sample.csv) and a brief note on configurable retention windows and customer-managed storage options. Highlights below: 

- Audit log sample: includes timestamp, request_id, model_name, redaction_flag, user_role, action, checksum. The sample has PHI fields redacted (***).
- Retention options:
  - Redwood-managed logs: configurable retention 90d / 180d / 13mo (archival to cold storage available)
  - Customer-managed logs: push to customer S3 (preferred for regulated flows); Redwood will sign an ACL and rotate export keys as required.
- Access controls: logs can be role-restricted; we support IAM-federated read-only roles + signed temporary access for audits.
- Evidence we can share now: SOC2 Type II executive summary, audit-log sample (redacted), architecture diagram for private VPC flow (link below). Full SOC2 report requires an NDA — can send via DocuSign link if needed.

Proposed updated MAP table (short):
- Data Classification & Retention — BlueHealth to confirm CSV by 2027-04-08; Redwood to provide redacted log sample & retention options by 2027-04-09. (Owners: BlueHealth / Monica)
- Audit Trail Evidence — Redwood to share SOC2 executive summary and architecture diagram by 2027-04-12. (Owner: Monica)
- PHI Endpoint Plan — BlueHealth to flag endpoints by 2027-04-08; Redwood Security (Neha) to propose keyflow and minimization approach by 2027-04-14. (Owner: BlueHealth / Neha)

Please review and confirm. If procurement needs the SOC2 earlier than 4/12, we can prioritize sending an NDA + limited disclosure via DocuSign.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
[Attachment: audit-log-sample.csv (text/csv, 12 KB)]
[Attachment: redwood_map_draft_v2.pdf (application/pdf, 428 KB)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Caroline Hayes <caroline@bluehealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Data-handling checkpoint — retention, logs & PHI scope

Caroline / team — quick note from security:

- Confirmed: Redwood supports TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest for customer data; customer-managed KMS is supported in the Private deployment model.
- For audit integrity we offer SHA256 checksums on exported logs plus an optional WORM-style bucket for immutability (customer-managed S3 recommended).
- Next step: I can run a lightweight architecture review focused on PHI ingress patterns and key management. To do this I need: the data flow diagram (we have one attached in the MAP draft) and the list of endpoints that will carry PHI.

If BlueHealth can confirm the endpoints and whether they'll accept a customer-managed S3 for logs by 2027-04-12, we can hit the MAP target of 2027-05-15.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Director, Applied Security | Redwood Inference
